explanations.answer: See the land given to Israel
explanations.explanation: That's the job, friend. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) Notice the word "given." The LORD calls it land He has given to the Israelites, and Moses gets to look at it from up there.

explanations.answer: Build an altar to the LORD
explanations.explanation: I get why an altar comes to mind, since mountains and altars go together in a lot of stories. But this time the LORD sends Moses up for a different reason. He says, "…see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) No bricks, no stones, just a long look.

Nope, this verse doesn't mention anyone waiting up there for Moses. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) What the LORD tells Moses to do on the mountain is see the land. No elders show up in the verse at all.

Ooh, I know why this one sounds right. A leader walks his people all that way, so you expect him to walk in with them. But God doesn't say that. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Seeing the land comes first, then Moses is gathered to his people. I think that's a heavy thing to hear.

Right, and it's a tender one. God doesn't say Moses will lead Israel into the land. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Moses gets to see it, and he is gathered to his people.

Aaron it is. God says Moses will be gathered to his people "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The word "brother" tells you this is family. Aaron comes up again in the very next verse, where God says "…both of you rebelled…" (Numbers 27:14).

Korah is a name that floats up, I get it, but it isn't the one God says here. God says, "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The verse names Moses' brother, so the name has to be Aaron. Korah isn't named anywhere in this passage.
Caleb is a good name to know, but he isn't the one here. God is talking about Moses' own brother. He says, "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Same family, same long road.

Yes, and God says it straight. He tells Moses, "…both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters." (Numbers 27:14) Both of them, Moses and Aaron. The text doesn't soften it, so I won't either.

This one is True, and it's a hard one to hear. God says, "…both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters." (Numbers 27:14) The "…both of you…" means Moses and Aaron. God says it plainly, so we take it plainly.

explanations.answer: A man to lead the congregation
explanations.explanation: That's it. Moses asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation…" (Numbers 27:16) He asks this right after hearing he'll be gathered to his people. I think his request shows how much he cares about who leads them next.

I bet plenty of us would ask for that one, me first. But Moses doesn't. He asks, "May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation…" (Numbers 27:16) His request is about who leads next, not about himself.

explanations.answer: A way into the land after all
explanations.explanation: Good guess, because that's what a lot of us would beg for. But the text doesn't have Moses asking that. He asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation…" (Numbers 27:16) His request is for the people's next leader.

Yes, sheep. Moses says he doesn't want the congregation of the LORD to be "…like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) It's a picture of people with no one to lead them. Matthew 9:36 describes the crowds with the same words, "…like sheep without a shepherd."

Soldiers is a fair guess, but it isn't the picture Moses uses. He says he doesn't want the congregation of the LORD to be "…like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) A shepherd is the picture he picks for a leader. I think it's a gentle one.

Travelers fits, I'll give you that, because Israel is definitely on a journey. But Moses uses a different picture. He says, "…so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) It's sheep, friend.

Spirit is right. God calls Joshua "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) That's the description God gives when He tells Moses to take Joshua son of Nun. Out of everything God could point to, it's the Spirit.

Strength is a natural guess, but it's not the word God uses. He says, "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) The thing God points to in Joshua is the Spirit. The verse never mentions strength.
Fire sounds mighty dramatic, I'll admit. But God doesn't call Joshua a man with fire in him. He says, "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) Save the fire for my ovens.

That's the one. God says, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) And Moses does just that. The text says he "…laid his hands on him and commissioned him…" (Numbers 27:23).
Oil does show up elsewhere in Scripture, so it's a smart guess. But God doesn't mention oil here. He says, "…lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) Hands, nothing poured.

A staff handoff would make a great picture, wouldn't it? But the text doesn't say that here. God's instruction is, "…lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) No staff is mentioned in this passage, and hands are what God names.

This one is False, friend. God wants it out in the open. He says, "Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight." (Numbers 27:19) Nothing private about it.

Right, False. Nothing happens in a back room here. God tells Moses, "Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight." (Numbers 27:19) That's out in the open, with the whole congregation there to see it.

explanations.answer: So the congregation will obey him
explanations.explanation: That's the reason God gives. He says, "Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) God ties the authority Moses confers to the whole congregation obeying Joshua. Moses gives some of his own, and that's the purpose.

explanations.answer: So Moses can rest on the mountain
explanations.explanation: The text never says that. God gives a different reason: "…so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) It's about the people following Joshua. Moses taking a nap doesn't come into it.

explanations.answer: So Joshua can judge every case
explanations.explanation: I see why it sounds right, since leaders handle a lot of cases. But the text doesn't give that reason. God says, "…so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) The goal is that the people obey.

Counsel, you got it. God says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) Eleazar the priest does the seeking, and he does it for Joshua. It all happens before the LORD.

Mercy is a lovely word, but it's not the one God uses here. He says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) The word in the verse is counsel. Eleazar the priest is the one who seeks it for Joshua.

Blessing is a nice thought, but it's not the word in this verse. God says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) The word is counsel. Eleazar the priest seeks it for Joshua.

True. The text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it tells what he did: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. He had just heard God say he'd be gathered to his people, so I think that's a lot to take in and still do.

This one is True. After God finishes speaking, the text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it tells what he did: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. After that he "…laid his hands on him and commissioned him…" (Numbers 27:23).
